name: Chinese Ten
description: Chinese Ten (Jiǎn Hóng Diǎn / 拣红点): Chinese fishing game. Play a card to capture a layout card (pairs sum to 10, or same rank for 10/J/Q/K); then flip one from deck. Related to Thai Red Frog Black Frog and Indonesian Main Merah.
alsoKnownAs: Gob Dum Gob Dang กบดำกบแดง

overview.description: Chinese Ten (Jiǎn Hóng Diǎn / 拣红点): Chinese fishing game. Play a card to capture a layout card (pairs sum to 10, or same rank for 10/J/Q/K); then flip one from deck. Related to Thai Red Frog Black Frog and Indonesian Main Merah.

history.origins: China. Jiǎn Hóng Diǎn (pick up red spots). Oriental fishing style: card flipped from deck after each play. Similar to Thai Gob Dum Gob Dang and Indonesian Main Merah.
timeline: 24 cards in play (24 ÷ number of players dealt)
Four cards face up in layout; capture by sum-10 or same rank

setup.players: 2, 3, or 4. Each gets 24÷n cards (e.g. 2p=12 each, 4p=6 each).
setup.deck: 52 cards. Numeral 1–9 capture by sum to 10; Ten and pictures capture same rank only.
setup.dealing: Deal 24÷n cards each. Four cards turned face up as initial layout. Rest face down.

rules.objective: Capture cards from the layout. Numeral cards capture one card that sums to 10 with them (A–9, e.g. 3 captures 7). Tens and pictures capture one card of same rank only. Each play or flip captures at most one card.
rules.gameplay: Turn: play one card from hand. If it captures a layout card, take both to your pile; else add your card to layout. Then flip top of deck: if it captures, take both; else add to layout. Next player.
keyRules: Capture: numeral + numeral = 10, or same rank for 10/J/Q/K
One card captures at most one layout card
After play and flip, turn passes
